doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

title: Touring Europe with Benny Goodman
summary: Ruth and Bucky name the Goodman tour of 26 European cities as their heyday; her mother minded the children and Ruth was homesick.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What was your best time? What was your heyday or is it now?
When we went six weeks to Europe with Benny [Goodman].

Bucky and I and the band. And my mother took care of the children. We lived across the street then. And I was so homesick. So I called her home from England, I said, “Ma, do you want me to come home? I’m here in London and I can get a flight home.” And she said, “Ruth stay. Have a good time, enjoy. We are fine.” She wouldn’t let me go home. I wanted to go home. I was homesick.
26 cities in Europe with an all-English band with Benny.
It was in the late 50s or early 60s?

They weren’t babies, but they went to school right here in town. And my mother loved it. And even the kids said they had such a good time with her. And they’ll never forget it. And six weeks — and it was really great. Benny was very nice to us. And he visited us after.
Yeah he came and slept here a few times.
